guide.summary: Paints cells as muddy sediment on the bottom of the dish.
guide.biology: Muddy bottoms hold food and hide small microbes, and chemicals and gases move through them very slowly.
guide.rules: Turns covered cells into sediment without removing any life, deposits or dissolved fields. Dissolved things spread a tenth as fast as in water (0.01 per tick) and gas exchange with the air is ten times slower. Sediment is drier than open water, so an organism that needs wetter cells is less suited to it. An attached organism whose record lists sediment as a surface can hold on to it. Each organism's recorded habitats decide whether it can live in sediment; one that cannot responds through ordinary suitability. No additional modeled reaction.
guide.example: Paint a sediment bed next to open water and watch oxygen and sugar creep into it slowly.
